text: When a Gowin matmul is feasible at 187 MHz/8 DSPs with the acc_out carry chain critical and acc_width already at its 24-bit minimum, do not scale to 16 DSPs by doubling pe_cols 4→8 with pipe_mul=1/reg_in=1/dsp_regs=out unless you also shorten the control path, because it drops Fmax to 153.5 MHz (−33.8 MHz) and adds 486 LUTs as in_valid/busy LUTs (1.03–1.25 ns logic + 2.57 ns route) become critical instead of the carry chain; if max_dsp=16 is binding, use a shallower row dimension to cut A-broadcast fanout and keep dsp_regs=out as carry-chain insurance.

When a Gowin DSP matmul is timing-limited by control/token routing such as in_valid→busy with 2.57 ns route and already meets frequency at 153.5 MHz, remove the A/B boundary input registers (reg_in false) while keeping DSP output registered, which raised fmax to 194.0 MHz (+40.4 MHz) with no LUT/DSP change and moved the critical path to the 5.16 ns acc_out carry chain.

On a Gowin matmul whose 24-bit LUT4 carry-chain accumulator is the critical path, flatten the PE array from 2x8 to 1x16 to delete row counter/broadcast logic, gaining 21.1 MHz (194.0->215.1 MHz) with +202 LUT and same 16 DSPs, because the accumulator path drops from 24 to 19 carry cells (5.16->4.65 ns).

When a 16-DSP matmul on Gowin is already timing-feasible with >50% slack and LUT-bound, reshape the PE array from 1x16 to 4x4 to cut the deepest skew/broadcast chain from 8 to 4, reducing LUT 1178→1167 at the same 16 DSPs while the accumulator carry chain grows 4.65→5.25 ns and Fmax falls 215→190 MHz, still feasible because the slack absorbs the carry-chain increase.

When a Gowin 16-DSP matmul at 4x4 is timing-limited by the accumulator carry chain (24-cell carry, 2.86 ns logic + 1.53 ns route) and LUT cost is 1167, do not transpose to 8x2 to save LUTs: it cuts 135 LUTs but drops Fmax from 190 to 125 MHz because the critical path shifts to c_row LUT routing (4.83 ns route of 7.97 ns total), so keep 4x4 or use 2x8 unless you can register c_row.

On a Gowin matmul with 16 DSPs where Fmax is limited by 32-bit accumulator carry-chain feedback, reshape 4x4 to 2x8 and shorten acc_width to 24 bits: the carry chain drops 31->19 cells and Fmax improves 157.2->205.3 MHz (+48.1 MHz), with LUTs falling 577 and DSPs unchanged at 16.

When a Gowin matmul with 16 DSPs is carry-chain-limited at 205.3 MHz, do not reshape from 2x8 to 4x4 and add pipe_mul=2/dsp_regs=out as a fallback; it dropped Fmax to 134.7 MHz (-70.6) and added 194 LUTs because the critical path moved to the tok_row/in_last/busy control path (7.42 ns) instead of the 4.87 ns accumulator carry chain.

When a Gowin matmul with acc-in-DSP is routing-limited through the in_last/busy LUTs, set pipe_mul from 2 to 0 and DSP output registers from out to none to remove the in_last stage, raising Fmax 134.7 to 157.5 MHz (+22.8) with LUTs 1169 to 1168 and DSPs unchanged at 16.

When a Gowin matmul is feasible but the critical path is a 24-bit DSP accumulator carry chain at 5.34 ns (187.3 MHz) while only 8 of 16 MULT18X18 are used, double the PE columns from 4 to 8 to fill the 16-DSP cap; this keeps the carry chain as the path but shortens its route 1.85→1.44 ns, raising Fmax to 205.3 MHz (+18 MHz) for +485 LUT and +8 DSP.

When a Gowin matmul at 16 DSPs is timing-limited by the 24-bit acc_out carry-chain feedback in a 2x8 PE array, flatten the array to 1x16 (rows 2→1, cols 8→16) to shorten the carry-chain route, gaining 2.9 MHz (205.3→208.2 MHz) at constant 16 DSPs for +202 LUT with no feasibility change.

When a Gowin 8-bit matmul at a 120 MHz floor is feasible and carry-chain-limited with all 16 DSPs, reshape the PE array from 1×16 to 4×4 to cut LUTs 1177→1168 at equal DSPs; Fmax drops 208.2→157.5 MHz (−50.7) as the critical path moves from the 24-bit accumulator carry-chain to busy/token LUT4 logic, which the 120 MHz target still absorbs.

When a Gowin matmul is LUT-heavy and feasible at 157 MHz with the critical path being a 32-bit accumulator carry chain (31 cells), shrink acc_width to 24 and reshape the PE array from 4x4 to 2x8 to cut the chain to 19 cells and shorten its routing, reaching 205 MHz (+48 MHz) with 577 fewer LUTs and DSP count unchanged at 16.

When a Gowin 16-DSP matmul is feasible but the 2x8 PE array's accumulator carry-chain dominates, flattening to 1x16 shaves carry-chain route from 1.44 to 1.37 ns and raises Fmax only 2.9 MHz for +202 LUTs with no DSP change, so avoid it unless LUT slack is ample—the 2.58 ns carry logic remains the bottleneck.

When a Gowin 16-DSP matmul at 1×16 PEs is feasible at 208 MHz and only LUT reduction remains, keep the 1×16 shape rather than reshaping to 4×4, because the 9-LUT saving drops Fmax to 157 MHz by moving the critical path from the acc_out carry chain to the shared busy-control LUT/routing.

When a Gowin matmul is already feasible with 16 DSPs at the max but LUT-limited at 1168 LUT / 157.5 MHz and its critical path is the 6.35 ns busy-control LUT4, re-aspect the PE array from 4x4 to 2x8 with reg_in=true so the A/B boundary registers absorb operand muxes, cutting 191 LUTs and raising fmax 7.4 MHz to 164.9 MHz as the path shifts to a 6.07 ns in_valid LUT4.

When a 2x8 matmul on Gowin is feasible at 164.9 MHz with 16 DSP and LUT is the only movable objective, do not transpose to 8x2: it kept 16 DSP/16 MAC but added 53 LUT and dropped Fmax to 132.3 MHz because the c_row LUT path's route delay grew to 4.35 ns; only transpose if you first prove LUT savings.

When a Gowin matmul at 8x2 with reg_in=false is routing-limited at 132.3 MHz by the c_row operand-select LUT4 (7.56 ns), switch to a 4x4 tile with reg_in=true to absorb the operand muxes, raising Fmax by +48.5 MHz to 180.8 MHz and cutting LUTs to 1167 versus 1168 for 4x4 reg_in=false (though +137 versus 8x2) with DSP unchanged, which shifts the critical path to the 24-bit acc_out carry chain (5.53 ns).

On a Gowin matmul already feasible at 180.8 MHz with the 24-bit acc_out carry chain critical and DSPs pinned at the 16 cap, don't reshape the PE array from 4x4 to 8x2 just to save LUTs: LUT drops 1167→1030 but the critical path moves to a 3-LUT c_row net (2.28 ns logic + 4.98 ns route = 8.12 ns) and Fmax falls to 123.1 MHz (-57.7 MHz).

When a 16-DSP Gowin matmul at the DSP/MAC cap is routing-limited by the c_row LUT4 broadcast (4.98 ns route in an 8.12 ns path, 123.1 MHz), switch PE packing from 8x2 to 16x1 and drop reg_in to move the critical path onto busy/out_row logic (6.90 ns), gaining +21.8 MHz to 144.9 MHz despite +95 LUT (1030 to 1125).

When a 4x4 matmul PE array is capped at 16 DSPs (max_dsp) with a 32-bit acc_out carry chain (31 cells, 5.5 ns) dominating the 157 MHz path, reshape to 2x8 and narrow acc_width to 24, which shortens the carry chain to 19 cells and lifts Fmax to 205 MHz (+48 MHz) while cutting 577 LUTs at unchanged 16 DSPs/16 MAC/cycle.

When feasible at 205 MHz with a 2x8 PE array and carry-chain-limited acc_out on Gowin matmul, keep the 2x8 layout instead of reshaping to 4x4, because the 4x4 change adds 193 LUTs and drops Fmax to 157 MHz (-47.9 MHz) by moving the critical path to the busy LUT4 control logic at unchanged 16 DSPs.

When a 4×4 Gowin matmul at the 16-DSP cap is LUT-bound at 157.5 MHz with a 6.35 ns tok_row→busy→busy path, reshape to 8×2 to cut LUTs 1168→1030 (−138) at the same 16 DSPs, accepting Fmax 132.3 MHz (−25.1) because the critical path shifts to a longer c_row LUT route (4.35 ns vs 3.3 ns).

For a 4x4 Gowin DSP matmul that is carry-chain-limited on the loop-carried accumulator, flatten to a 1x16 PE row and narrow the accumulator from 32 to 24 bits to cut the carry chain from 31 to 19 cells, raising Fmax from 157.2 to 208.2 MHz (+51 MHz) with the same 16 DSPs and 375 fewer LUTs.

When a Gowin matmul uses all 16 DSPs and is timing-limited by the 32-bit accumulator carry chain, reshape the PE array from 4x4 to 2x8 and take acc_width to 24-bit to cut carry-chain cells 31->19 and LUTs by 202, but expect Fmax to stay flat or drop slightly (208.2->205.3 MHz) because the carry-chain route delay still dominates the critical path.

Keep the 2x8 PE shape for a 16-DSP matmul that is already feasible at 205 MHz with the accumulator carry-chain critical, rather than reshaping to 4x4—DSP stays 16 but the busy-control LUT4 path becomes critical (6.35 ns, 3.3 ns route), cutting Fmax to 157 MHz and adding 193 LUTs.

For a 16-DSP Gowin matmul timing-limited by a 3-LUT busy/control path at 157 MHz, reshape the PE array from 4x4 to 2x8 and add reg_in plus a DSP output register to cut the critical path to a single LUT4, reaching 187.9 MHz (+30.5 MHz) with 192 fewer LUTs (1168->976) at the same 16 DSPs.

On a Gowin 16-DSP matmul at 187.9 MHz where the DFF-tok_row-to-LUT4-c_row path burns 3.37 ns in routing, flatten the 2x8 PE array to 1x16 and set pipe_mul=1, raising Fmax to 206.2 MHz (+18.3 MHz) at +202 LUT and no DSP by shortening the row-control route and moving the critical path to the 24-cell acc_out carry chain.

On Gowin 1x16 matmul at ~206 MHz limited by the 24-bit accumulator carry-chain (24 cells, 2.78 ns logic + 1.22 ns route), keep the DSP output/pipeline registers because removing them (pipe_mul 1→0, dsp_regs out→none) saved only 2 LUTs and 0 DSPs while dropping Fmax to ~205 MHz (-0.9 MHz) as the path merely shifted to a 19-cell carry-chain.

When a 4x4 matmul PE array on Gowin is feasible at 157.2 MHz but timing-limited by a 32-bit accumulator carry-chain (31 cells, 5.5 ns of 6.36 ns path) with DSPs already at 16, reshape to 1x16 and narrow the accumulator to 24 bits to cut the carry chain to 19 cells and its route from 2.24 to 1.37 ns, yielding 208.2 MHz (+51 MHz) and 375 fewer LUTs at the same DSP count.

When a Gowin matmul with 16 DSPs is already timing-limited by a 19-cell accumulator carry chain, reshaping 2x8->1x16 saves 202 LUTs but lowers Fmax by 2.9 MHz because the carry chain remains critical and its route lengthens, so do it only to relieve LUT pressure, not for speed.

When a Gowin matmul is feasible at 205 MHz with 16 DSPs at the cap and carry-chain critical (19-cell acc_out, 4.02 ns), do not reshape the PE array from 2x8 to 4x4: it adds 193 LUTs and drops Fmax to 157 MHz by moving the critical path to a 3.3 ns LUT4 busy route, so keep the 2x8 shape and shorten the accumulator carry chain instead.

When a Gowin matmul saturates all 16 MULT18X18s at 157.5 MHz with a 4x4 PE grid and its critical path is the tok_row->busy LUT4->busy DFF route (6.35 ns), reshape to a 1x16 PE column and enable pipe_mul, reg_in, and the DSP output register to break the combinational DSP-to-adder route, moving the critical path to the 24-bit acc carry chain (4.85 ns) and raising Fmax by 48.8 MHz to 206.2 MHz at the same 16 DSPs and only +10 LUTs.

When a Gowin matmul is DSP-capped at 16 DSPs and timing-limited by the 24-bit accumulator carry-chain (4.85 ns total: 24 cells, 2.78 ns logic + 1.22 ns route), skip pipe_mul/dsp_reg retiming moves—pipe_mul [1,0] with dsp_regs out→none only cut 2 LUTs and cost 0.9 MHz (206.2→205.3 MHz)—because the carry-chain feedback remains the critical loop (4.87 ns, 19 cells, 2.58 ns logic + 1.44 ns route), not the multiplier pipeline or DSP output register.

When a Gowin matmul is DSP-capped at 16 MULT18X18 and its 24-bit accumulator carry-chain (acc_width already at the 2*8+8 minimum) is critical, reshape the PE array to 1x16 and add boundary/input registers to cut LUTs 1176->977 at constant DSP=16, accepting fmax 205->165 MHz as the critical path moves to tok_row->in_valid->busy, because only LUT/congestion reduction remains—use it only as an area fallback above the 120 MHz floor.

When a Gowin 4x4 matmul saturates 16 DSPs and is timing-limited by the 32-bit accumulator carry-chain (31 cells, 3.26 ns logic + 2.24 ns route, 157.2 MHz), reshape to 1x16 and reduce acc_width to 24 to shorten the carry-chain to 19 cells (2.58 ns logic + 1.37 ns route), yielding 208.2 MHz at the same 16 DSP and -375 LUT.

When a 4x4, 16-DSP Gowin matmul is carry-chain-limited at 208.2 MHz, shorten the accumulator width instead of flattening to 1x16, since flattening at constant 16 DSP moved the critical path from the 19-cell carry chain to the busy control LUT4 (3.3 ns route) and cut Fmax to 157.5 MHz (-50.7 MHz).

When a 4x4 matmul on Gowin saturates its 16 DSPs but is timing-limited at 157.5 MHz by the 32-bit acc_out carry chain, flatten the array to 2x8 and drop acc_width to 24 to cut the chain from 31 to 19 cells and shorten its route (+47.9 MHz, reaching 205.3 MHz at LUT -193 and unchanged DSP).
